# Kenneth Loi

> Incoming graduate student in UC Berkeley Biophysics in the Doudna Lab, focused on programmable biology, RNA-guided systems, structural discovery, selfish genetic elements, and computational acceleration for biological discovery and design.

## Canonical Links

- Website: /
- Google Scholar: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=t4pJa5EAAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao

- Email: mailto:kenjmloi@berkeley.edu

## Research Themes

- Programmable biology: designing and reprogramming molecular systems for detection, regulation, and computation.
- Structural discovery: studying structures conserved across hundreds of millions of years.
- Selfish genes: studying genetic conflict to understand biomolecular innovations.
- Computational acceleration: leveraging computational techniques to discover and design new biology.

## Selected Works

- A Noncontiguous Code for RNA-Guided DNA Recognition Preceded CRISPR. Preprint, 2026. Co-first author. https://www.lifescience.net/preprints/15627/a-noncontiguous-code-for-rna-guided-dna-recognitio/
- Triplex formation drives noncontiguous VIPR RNA-guided DNA recognition. Preprint, 2026. https://www.lifescience.net/preprints/15628/triplex-formation-drives-noncontiguous-vipr-rna-gu/
- A miniature CRISPR-Cas10 enzyme confers immunity by an inverse signaling pathway. Nature, 2025. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09569-9
- Structure-guided discovery of ancestral CRISPR-Cas13 ribonucleases. Science, 2024. https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adq0553
- Eukaryotic RNA-guided endonucleases evolved from a unique clade of bacterial enzymes. Nucleic Acids Research, 2023. https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/51/22/12414/7424439
